title: Six-minute walk test
what: You walk along a hallway for 6 minutes at your own pace. The test measures how many meters you walked and how your pulse and oxygen change.
why: For lung and heart conditions, to check your stamina, choose treatment, or see how well it works.
duration: usually 20 to 30 minutes including rest; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: If you get chest pain or feel very dizzy with activity
If you use oxygen, a cane, or a walker
If your joints or legs hurt

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light meal a couple of hours before the test. Do not come hungry.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: You usually take your medicines as always. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Exercise
prepare.text: No exercise for 2 hours before the test.

bring: Your cane or walker, if you use one
Your inhaler, if you have one
steps: You rest sitting down for about 10 minutes
Your blood pressure, pulse, and finger oxygen are checked
You walk back and forth along the hallway for 6 minutes
You can slow down or stop if it is hard
Every minute, you are told how much time is left
After the test, your pulse and oxygen are checked again
feel: You may get short of breath and tired
Your legs get tired. That is normal
after: Sit for a few minutes after the test
The result, the distance you walked, is given right away
Your doctor will compare it with past tests
red_flags: Chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or dizziness during the test: stop right away and tell staff
Chest pain that does not go away with rest: call emergency services

faq.a: No. Walk fast, but at a pace that is comfortable for you. Running is not allowed.
Yes. Rest and keep going when you can. The clock keeps running.

reminders.text: Six-minute walk test tomorrow. Wear comfortable shoes and have a light breakfast.
